metaData.originalTitle: 对话 Lucius 赵赫：AI 员工的本质，是一份有 SLA 的劳动合同
metaData.title: Dialogue with Lucius Zhao He: The Essence of an AI Employee is an Employment Contract with an SLA
metaData.oneSentenceSummary: Lucius founder Zhao He believes that a true AI employee requires an 'employment contract' with an SLA, where the core is delivering deterministic results rather than capabilities, by building an independent Context Layer to manage the organization's tacit knowledge, state, and permissions, achieving AI in the Loop automation.
metaData.summary: This article is an in-depth conversation between Founder Park and Lucius founder Zhao He. Lucius is a company focused on enterprise-grade AI employees, but its core is not providing general AI capabilities; rather, it builds an organizational orchestration system called the 'Context Layer.' Zhao He argues that the biggest difference between AI and human employees is that the former must deliver deterministic results, thus requiring a clear 'employment contract' to define responsibilities, permissions, and SLAs. The article elaborates on Lucius's technical architecture, including an independent knowledge engine, state machine, and scheduler, which together enable the proactive collection, cleaning, and reuse of organizational context. Zhao He also shares his thoughts on the future form of AI employees, suggesting that organizations will eventually evolve into a 'pilot' model, where humans shift from executors to supervisors. He also candidly discusses the challenges faced by the team, such as engineering difficulty, market education costs, and team mindset management.

mainPoints.point: The core of an AI employee is delivering deterministic results, not providing uncertain capabilities.
mainPoints.explanation: Zhao He believes the ToB market requires predictable, quantifiable delivery, not a tool that users need to debug themselves. Lucius ensures delivery quality by setting clear SLAs for each AI role, which is its fundamental difference from traditional AI tools.

mainPoints.point: The Context Layer is the key to truly integrating AI into an organization; it solves the problem of 'what the system should do now.'
mainPoints.explanation: Unlike traditional knowledge bases or wikis, the Context Layer manages not only static knowledge but also dynamic states, user profiles, workflows, and permissions. It enables AI to understand the current context, make correct judgments, and take actions, rather than just providing information.

mainPoints.point: Signing an 'employment contract' for AI employees is the institutional guarantee for delivery, achieved through clear role boundaries and permission control.
mainPoints.explanation: When Lucius's AI employees join a work group, they clearly state their scope of responsibilities. Tasks outside this scope require administrator 'sign-off' authorization. This mechanism ensures AI behavior is controllable, preventing chaos and delivery failures caused by unclear responsibilities.

mainPoints.point: 'Full replacement' by AI is not just a technical issue but also an institutional one, requiring incremental trust-building.
mainPoints.explanation: Zhao He believes that even with mature technology, full automation requires supporting systems (e.g., accountability, risk control) and the gradual building of human trust. Lucius adopts a phased strategy, starting with low-risk tasks and progressively expanding AI's decision-making authority.

mainPoints.point: Lucius's Harness is its core barrier, not the underlying LLM.
mainPoints.explanation: Harness comprises four layers: context assembly, behavior constraints, state management, and observability. It is a code-enforced enterprise governance framework. LLMs can be swapped, but Harness embodies the understanding of enterprise scenarios and is the true moat.

keyQuotes: ToB must deliver deterministic results, not deliver a capability.
AI cannot be responsible for the final profit margin. As long as someone has to backstop it, you cannot achieve 100% automation. This is not a technical issue; it's an institutional issue.
Every role we deliver is because we control the SLA and take responsibility for the result.
Knowledge bases, wikis, and enterprise search solve 'what the system knows'; the Context Layer solves 'what the system should do now.'
The biggest fear is not running fast enough, but running in the wrong direction. One misstep and you lose three months of progress.

relatedArticles.title: The First Java Harness Framework Arrives: AgentScope Brings OpenClaw to Enterprise Distributed Scenarios
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: AgentScope Java 1.1.0 is officially released, packaging engineering capabilities such as workspace, pluggable file system, memory management, and sub-agent orchestration through the Harness Framework, solving five core obstacles that prevent personal assistant models like OpenClaw from being deployed in enterprise-level distributed scenarios.

relatedArticles.title: The 'AI Employee' Track, Hotter Than OpenClaw, Has a New Champion | AI New Arrivals
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article provides an in-depth review of GenSpark 4.0, arguing that it leads the 'AI employee' track with its product philosophy. By offering a one-stop work environment, extensive tool integrations, and customizable Skill workflows, it achieves a category shift from AI tools to AI employees.

relatedArticles.title: Notion Custom Agents Retrospective: Rewritten 5 Times in Three Years, One of the Most Successful New Features in Notion's History
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article, based on an in-depth interview with Notion AI's Head of Engineering Sarah Sachs and Tech Lead Simon Last, thoroughly reviews the winding development journey of Notion Custom Agents from 2022 to the present, its core design philosophy, team management principles, and forward-looking thoughts on the future of AI Agents.

relatedArticles.title: The OpenClaw Ecosystem is Exploding: We Deconstructed Over 40 Related Products on Product Hunt
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article provides an in-depth deconstruction of the AI Agent ecosystem built around the OpenClaw framework, covering five core tracks—social, memory, deployment, security, and hardware—revealing the trend of the internet shifting from "serving humans" to "serving Agents."

relatedArticles.title: Agent Infra Practice Review: How Kimi Built the Database Service Behind Its Agent
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: PingCAP CTO Huang Dongxu reviews the practice of TiDB Cloud providing database support for Kimi K2.6 Agent website building service, revealing the core challenges and architectural choices of data infrastructure in the Agent era.

relatedArticles.title: The Best Way for Humans and AI Agents to Collaborate Hasn't Been Invented Yet | A Conversation with Paperboy
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: A conversation with Paperboy founder John Yang and founding engineer Jett Chen, delving into three major pain points of current Agent product forms (Session-based, Reactive, and lack of Memory), and sharing practices and explorations in collecting user context at the OS level to build personalized Agents.

relatedArticles.title: Prompt Engineering and Context Engineering are Outdated: It's the Era of Harness Engineering
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article introduces Harness Engineering, a new paradigm in AI development, emphasizing that the core work of engineers is shifting from writing code to designing operating environments and feedback loops for AI Agents.

relatedArticles.title: Conversation with CREAO: A 20-Person Team, Launching 8 Features Daily — Before Pivoting the Product, We First Pivoted the Organization
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article is an in-depth interview with AI startup CREAO, revealing its transition from a Vibe Coding tool to a Super Agent platform. The core lies in a thorough AI Native organizational transformation, delegating 95% of development work to AI, achieving extreme iteration speed and product pivot capability.
